Electrical panel constraint modeling was added to ResStock via OpenStudio-HPXML measures in 2025 to assess whether the existing panel has enough capacity or breaker space to accommodate new loads from an energy retrofit. For details on panel constraint modeling, refer to the ResStock Technical Reference Guide (Reyna, Fontanini and Parker, et al. 2025). This measure does not introduce new electrical loads or circuits, so it has no impact on the electrical panel. However, electrical panel metrics are included as a standard output for this and all other envelope measures. Any panel constraints appearing in the upgrade results reflect pre-existing conditions, as this measure does not worsen them. 3.1 OpenStudio-HPXML Overview The ResStock building stock energy model includes conditional probability distributions of building characteristics that represent the U.S. residential building stock (Reyna, Fontanini and Present, et al. 2024). These distributions are sampled to create a synthetic stock, with each sample an option for each characteristic. ResStock uses the OpenStudio-HPXML (OS-HPXML) workflow to translate these dwelling characteristics into building models that can be simulated via OpenStudio® and EnergyPlus® using an HPXML (Home Performance eXtensible Markup Language) file. The state of the OpenStudio-HPXML repository at the time the ResStock 2025 Release 1 dataset was created is available on the NLR ResStock Resources page on GitHub.5 3.2 ResStock Inputs for Advanced Air Sealing with Drill-and-Fill Wall Insulation Building characteristics are assigned in ResStock and then translated into more detailed OS- HPXML arguments that describe a ResStock parameter.
